items.stem: A bulb is lit by one battery. A second battery is added in series. What happens to the bulb?
options: It stays just the same as before

explain.why: More batteries in series push more current.
The extra battery gives more energy.
The bulb still has a complete circuit.

solution: More cells in series give a larger current, so the bulb is brighter.

items.stem: A second bulb is added in series to a circuit with one battery and one bulb. What happens to the first bulb?

explain.why: The battery now has to light two bulbs.

solution: More bulbs in series make the current smaller.

items.stem: Circuits A and B each have a single bulb. Which bulb is brighter?

explain.why: A has fewer cells, so a smaller current.
The two circuits have different numbers of cells.

solution: Circuit B has two cells in series, so more current flows.

items.stem: What happens to the current when more bulbs are added in series?

explain.why: More bulbs make it harder for the current.

solution: More bulbs in one loop make the current smaller.

items.stem: A student places a coin in the gap of a circuit and the bulb lights. Which statement about the coin is correct?

explain.why: An insulator would stop the bulb lighting.
The coin does not supply energy.

solution: The bulb lit, so the coin conducts.

items.stem: A rubber band is placed in the gap of a circuit. The bulb does not light. What does this show?
options: The rubber band is a conductor
The rubber band is an insulator

explain.why: A conductor would let the bulb light.
The test does not show this.
The test does not show this.

solution: Rubber does not let electricity through.

items.stem: Metals are good conductors of electricity. Which of the following is a metal?
options: A glass marble for a game
A rubber ball for a game
A wooden block for a game
solution: Steel is a metal.

items.stem: Two cells are joined in series. How does this compare with using one cell?
options: The bulb gets less energy and is dimmer
The bulb gets more energy and is brighter
The bulb is the same brightness
solution: Two cells in series push a bigger current.

items.stem: Which change will make the bulb in a series circuit brighter?

explain.why: Wire length is not the answer.
An open switch turns the bulb off.

solution: More cells give a larger current.

items.stem: The table shows the brightness of a bulb for different numbers of cells in series. What can be concluded?
options: The more cells in series, the brighter the bulb
The more cells in series, the dimmer the bulb
The number of cells does not affect the bulb
The bulb is brightest with one cell

explain.why: The bulb got brighter with more cells.
With one cell it was dim.

solution: Brightness rose with each extra cell.

items.stem: A student wants a bulb to be brighter without changing the bulb or the wires. What can she do?
options: Add a switch to the circuit

explain.why: A switch does not change brightness.
This will not make the bulb brighter.

solution: More cells in series give more current.

items.stem: Which of the following will make the bulb in a series circuit dimmer?
options: Removing a bulb from the circuit

explain.why: A switch does not change brightness.

solution: More bulbs in series make the current smaller.

items.stem: A circuit has two cells and two bulbs in series. Which change will make the bulbs brighter?
options: Adding a third cell in series
Adding a third bulb in series
Taking out one of the cells

explain.why: A switch does not change brightness.

solution: More cells in series give more current.

items.stem: The table shows what happened when different objects were placed in the gap of a circuit. Which object is most likely to be made of a metal?

explain.why: R did not light the bulb.
S did not light the bulb.
U did not light the bulb.

solution: Only T lit the bulb, so it is a conductor, most likely a metal.

items.stem: A bulb lights when a pencil lead is in the gap but not when a wooden pencil casing is in the gap. Which is the best conclusion?
options: The lead is a conductor and the wood is an insulator
The lead is an insulator and the wood is a conductor

explain.why: The wood did not light the bulb.

solution: Only the lead lit the bulb.

items.stem: Which of the following would be best for making the outer cover of an electric plug?
options: Copper, because it is a good conductor
Plastic, because it is an insulator
Iron, because it is very strong

explain.why: A conductor on the outside would be unsafe.
Iron conducts electricity, so it is unsafe.
Aluminium conducts electricity, so it is unsafe.

solution: The cover should not let electricity pass to the user.

items.stem: A series circuit has one cell and three bulbs. Two bulbs are replaced by wires. What happens to the brightness of the remaining bulb?

explain.why: Fewer bulbs mean a bigger current.

solution: With fewer bulbs in series, the current is larger.

items.stem: Circuits X and Y each have one bulb. X has two cells in series and Y has one cell. A second bulb is added in series in both circuits. Which statement is correct?
options: The bulbs in both circuits become brighter
The bulbs in X become brighter and those in Y become dimmer
The bulbs in both circuits become dimmer

explain.why: More bulbs in series make the current smaller.
Adding a bulb has the same kind of effect in both.
The current falls in both circuits.

solution: More bulbs in series make the current smaller in both circuits.

items.stem: A student sets up the circuit shown, with two bulbs in separate paths and one cell. He says the bulbs will be as bright as a single bulb on the same cell. Is he correct?
options: No, they will be dimmer because they share the cell
Yes, each bulb is joined straight across the cell

explain.why: There is no extra energy for each bulb.
They are not in the same path.

solution: Bulbs in separate paths are each as bright as a single bulb.

items.stem: A student tests whether a spoon conducts electricity. She uses a circuit with a battery and a bulb and puts the spoon in the gap. The bulb does not light. She is surprised because the spoon looks like metal. What is the most likely reason?
options: The spoon is a metal conductor
The spoon has a plastic paint layer
The battery is far too strong

explain.why: A conductor would let the bulb light, so something is blocking the current.
A strong battery would light the bulb.
The bulb did not light at all.

solution: A paint or plastic layer blocks the current.

items.stem: The table shows the brightness of a bulb with different numbers of cells in series. How bright is the bulb likely to be with 4 cells?
options: Dimmer than it was with 3 cells

explain.why: The pattern is brighter with more cells.

solution: Brightness rises with every extra cell.

items.stem: A switch is added in series to a circuit with one cell and one bulb, and the switch is closed. What happens to the brightness of the bulb?

explain.why: A switch does not add energy.
A closed switch does not reduce the current.
A closed switch keeps the circuit complete.

solution: A closed switch only completes the circuit.

items.stem: Which row shows two materials that are both good conductors of electricity?
solution: Both are metals.

items.stem: A student wants to find out whether the number of bulbs in series affects the brightness. Which is the best way?
options: Use more cells each time a bulb is added
Use one cell and add bulbs one by one
Use a different bulb each time

explain.why: The number of cells must be kept the same.
The bulb type must be kept the same.

solution: Only the number of bulbs should change.

items.stem: Circuit A has one cell and one bulb. Circuit B has three cells and three bulbs in series. How does the brightness of each bulb in B compare with the bulb in A?

explain.why: The three bulbs share the three cells.
Each bulb still gets about one cell's worth.

solution: Each bulb in B gets about as much as the bulb in A.

items.stem: Why do torches often use two or more cells in series?
options: To make the bulb much dimmer

explain.why: The number of wires is not the reason.
This has no link to the cells.

solution: More cells give a bigger current.

items.stem: A steel nail and a plastic cap are tested one at a time in the gap of a circuit with a cell and a bulb. Which result is expected?
options: The bulb lights with the cap but not with the nail
The bulb lights with the nail but not with the cap

explain.why: Plastic is an insulator and steel is a conductor.

solution: Steel conducts and plastic does not.

items.stem: Which of the following circuits will have the dimmest bulbs?
options: Three cells with three bulbs in series
One cell with three bulbs in series

explain.why: This has about one cell per bulb.
One bulb gets all the cell's energy.

solution: The fewest cells for the most bulbs.

items.stem: Which of the following circuits will have the brightest bulbs?
options: One cell with three bulbs in series
Two cells with two bulbs in series
One cell with two bulbs in series

explain.why: Each bulb has about one cell's worth.

solution: The most cells for the fewest bulbs.

items.stem: The bulbs in circuits A and B are the same. How does the brightness of the bulb in A compare with a bulb in B?
options: The bulb in A is brighter
The bulb in B is brighter
The bulbs in B do not light

explain.why: In a parallel circuit each bulb has its own path to the battery.
Each path has the same current as in A.
Each path in B is a complete loop with the battery, so both bulbs light.

solution: In B each bulb has its own path, so it is as bright as the bulb in A.
